## Natural history notes

A small aquatic crambid moth characterized by pale tan to whitish wings with delicate brown markings, with males often more strongly patterned than the plainer females. In Florida, it is found around ponds, lakes, marshes, canals, ditches, and other freshwater wetlands where waterlilies, lotus, and other floating aquatic plants occur. Adults are mostly nocturnal and may come to lights near water, while the aquatic caterpillars feed on waterlily leaves and bore into stems or petioles, helping connect wetland plant growth with aquatic and shoreline food webs.
